To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tyr985 of the leptin (LRb) receptor binds the LRb-induced protein SOCS3 to mediate feedback inhibition.
SOCS3 is a feedback inhibitor of LRb signaling that binds to phosphorylated Tyr-985 of LRb.
SOCS3 mediates feedback inhibition on the leptin receptor via Tyr985.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of signal transduction by the cytokine leptin.
the molecular mechanisms by which the leptin receptor transmits intracellular signals.
the mechanisms of feedback inhibition of LR signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tyr985 of LRβ is involved in the negative regulation of the LRβ signaling via SOCS3.
SOCS3 is a negative feedback inhibitor of leptin receptor signaling, and that SOCS3 binds to phosphorylated Tyr 985 of the leptin-receptor.
SOCS3 mediates feedback inhibition via Tyr985 during leptin signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tyr985 of LR mediates both positive and negative signaling during acute stimulation and that SOCS3 mediates feedback inhibition by Tyr985 during chronic stimulation.
Tyr985 of LR mediates both SHP2 binding and ER activation, as well as the feedback inhibition of LR signaling by SOCS3.
Tyr985 of the leptin (OB) receptor (LR) mediates both SHP-2-dependent activation of the ERK kinases, and SHP-2-independent inhibition of LR signaling by SOCS3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Tyr985 of the leptin and erythropoietins receptors mediates the negative feedback inhibition of signaling by the receptor via binding of SOCS3.
SOCS3 binds to the leptin receptor at Tyr985 and inhibits the leptin receptor by binding to Tyr985.
Tyr985 of LR is not only a docking site for SHP-2 but also for SOCS3, and that SOCS3 is a negative regulator of the LRb signal transduction pathway.
